feedback.problem: A point $P$ has Cartesian coordinates $(4,-1).$ What are the polar coordinates of $P?$ Round your answer to two decimal places where necessary.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we determine $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{(-1)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16+1} \\  & =\sqrt{17} \\  & =4.123\,10… \\  & ≈4.12\end{aligned}
$$

We then compute the reference angle ${\theta }_{R}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{R} & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{-1}{4})| \\  & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-0.25)| \\  & =|-0.244\,97…| \\  & ≈0.244\,97\end{aligned}
$$

Since the point lies in the fourth quadrant, we subtract the reference angle from $2\pi ,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta  & =2\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =2\pi -0.244\,97 \\  & ≈6.04\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the polar coordinates of $P$ are $(4.12,6.04),$ rounded to two decimal places.
